preamble.summary:
At the release cut, phax's release notes are written from what the release's runs delivered: each completed spec with its guiding rule and the surfaces it changed, each plan without a spec, the commits made outside any run, and the release's upgrade steps. The cut writes them to `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md` in the release commit, the same file becomes the GitHub release body and a page of the docs site, and `pnpm release:notes` previews them at any time without writing anything.

This is repository tooling only: nothing under `src/` changes, and no phax command, format or schema is added. There is no source spec. No phase edits a skill, so the run needs no `--allow-skill-edits`.

Four phases, every commit green:

- phase-01 (oracle phase): the note builder's input types, a stub, and the oracles that freeze the Markdown layout from made-up inputs.
- phase-02 (its discharge): `renderReleaseNotes`, the pure builder in `scripts/releaseNotes.ts`.
- phase-03: `scripts/release-notes.ts` reads the git range, the plans, the specs and `docs/upgrading.md`. `pnpm release:notes` previews the notes, the cut writes `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md`, and CI's checkout fetches the history and tags that its release rehearsal now reads.
- phase-04: the release workflow publishes the file as the GitHub release body, the docs site renders one page per release, `docs/release.md` documents it, and `NEXT_STEPS.md` drops the item.

Operator notes:

- Never run `scripts/release.sh`, and cut no release from a phase. The phases exercise the cut and the notes on temporary copies and fixture repositories only.
- Land this run before cutting 0.28.0, so that 0.28.0 is the first release cut with the script. After the merge, run `pnpm release:notes` on main and read the notes before cutting.
- 0.28.0's notes, built on main at 5300b3fe plus this plan's run, should read as below. The `before` and `after` blocks hold the sidecar's text verbatim; here they are shortened to `…`, as is the Upgrading section after its first bullet. Fixes shows the one `fix:` commit without trailers known at 5300b3fe; any other in the range is listed the same way. No warning is expected.

## Plans

### Release notes from specs

At the release cut, phax's release notes are written from what the release's runs delivered: each completed spec with its guiding rule and the surfaces it changed, each plan without a spec, the commits made outside any run, and the release's upgrade steps. The cut writes them to `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md` in the release commit, the same file becomes the GitHub release body and a page of the docs site, and `pnpm release:notes` previews them at any time without writing anything.

preamble.requiredCommandsNote: No new command is needed. The phases run the `standard` gate profile's commands and commands `phax.json` already allows: `git log` to read history, and `pnpm exec tsx scripts/release-notes.ts` to preview the notes. Agents are granted `pnpm exec tsx`, not the new `pnpm release:notes` script, so they use the `pnpm exec tsx` form. `phax.json` needs no change. No phase edits a skill, so the run needs no `--allow-skill-edits`.
technicalArbitrations: The previous release is the ledger's greatest release below the version being noted (`packages/schemas/releases.json`, read with `readLedger`), and the range starts at its tag `v<previous>`. A missing tag is refused, and the refusal names `git fetch --tags`. A version with no ledger release below it is refused too. The ledger has held every release since 0.17.0, so no first-release mode is built. Loss (against taking the last tag): the notes need the previous release's tag in the clone, so a shallow clone cannot build them. In exchange, a stray or out-of-order tag can never move the range.

The cut builds the notes before its first write. `cutRelease(repoRoot, version, notes)` takes a function and calls it after its existing refusals and its new refusal of an existing `docs/releases/<version>.md`. It writes the returned Markdown after the ledger and lists the path among the changed ones, so `release.sh` stages it with the rest. The cut's own entry builds the notes from git: it loads `scripts/release-notes.ts` with a dynamic import, so the two scripts form no static import cycle. Tests pass a function instead. CI rehearses the cut on every push and pull request, so `ci.yml`'s checkout sets `fetch-depth: 0`, and every pull request then proves that the opened version's notes build. Loss: `release-cut.ts --root` no longer dry-runs on a plain copy of the files, only on a clone with the tags, and CI checks out the whole history on every run.

The published-format surfaces are the `file:` elements, since the phax-spec skill gives `file:` to whatever a reading tool or person consumes. The notes keep the `cli:`, `config:` and `file:` elements, and leave out `api:`, `package:` and `internal:`. Loss: a `file:` element that names an internal file, such as a skill, is shown too, and a `package:` element of the schemas package is not.

Reading the documents:
- A plan's status, `source-spec` and `completes-spec` come from its frontmatter, through `readPlanFrontmatter` (`src/domain/artifact/lineage.ts`).
- Its title and first paragraph come from its plan.md body: the text of the first level-1 heading, and the source of the first paragraph after it.
- Its sidecar, when it has one, is decoded through `readDocumentSidecar`, and only to get the run short name.
- A spec is looked up at its `source-spec` path, then at `archivePathFor` of that path. Its sidecar is decoded through `readDocumentSidecar`, which lifts older shapes as phax does.
- A spec without a sidecar is announced by its `# ` title alone, with one warning.

Loss: a hand-written spec gets no guiding rule and no surfaces in the notes.

The site renders one page per release. Each `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md` becomes `/releases/<X-Y-Z>`, with dots turned into hyphens as in the preview alias, titled `phax <X.Y.Z>`. The pages are listed newest first in a `Releases` sidebar group with its own nav entry. The site build generates them from the files present, so no release edits `site/pages.ts`. A file under `docs/releases/` that is not named `X.Y.Z.md` is a build finding. The site still refuses raw HTML, except the builder's `<details>`/`<summary>` blocks in release notes, which become Rspress `:::details <summary text>` containers. Loss: no single page lists every release's notes, and the fold on the site depends on Rspress's container syntax rather than the HTML GitHub shows.

One oracle pair, phase-01 to phase-02, covers the note builder. Its input is decoded facts and its output is a Markdown document that the layout above states exactly. So `renderReleaseNotes` is a stable entry the oracles can call before the code exists, and the layout is frozen before the code that writes it. The reader (phase-03) is not paired: its behaviour depends on git and on the documents on disk, so it is tested in-phase on fixture repositories. Loss: one more phase and gate than a three-phase plan.

The release workflow checks the notes before anything is published. A `Verify the release notes` step (id `notes`), placed after `Prepare npm wrapper`, refuses a missing or empty `docs/releases/${RELEASE_TAG#v}.md` and outputs its path. The GitHub Release step reads that file with `body_path` and no longer sets `generate_release_notes`. `.github/release.yml`, whose categories only GitHub's generated notes read, is deleted. Loss: a release commit without its notes file now fails the workflow before the deploy, where GitHub would have generated notes.

phases.title: Oracles for the release notes builder
phases.objective: The release notes builder gets a contract before it gets code. `scripts/releaseNotes.ts` declares the input types and a stub of `renderReleaseNotes`. Oracle tests, marked as expected failures, state the exact Markdown, warnings and refusals the builder must produce from made-up inputs.
detailedInstructions: Read the layout arbitration and the 0.28.0 example in the plan preamble first: the oracles encode them byte for byte.
The stub's body throws `new Error("renderReleaseNotes is not implemented")`. Keep the parameter named `_input`: `pnpm test:type` typechecks the scripts that tests import, under `noUnusedParameters`.

Create `tests/unit/releaseNotes/inputs.ts` with the made-up inputs and their expected outputs, exported for the test file. Use made-up versions (`4.2.0`, previous `4.1.0`), the repository `https://github.com/acme/tool`, made-up paths under `docs/plans/archive/` and `docs/specs/archive/`, and 40-character hex hashes. Write every expected document as a literal array of lines joined with a newline and ending with an empty line. Never compute one by calling a helper.

Create `tests/unit/releaseNotes.test.ts`. Mark every test `it.fails`, the Vitest expected-failure marker that `examples/vitest-oracles/` requires. Never use `skip`, `todo`, `only`, `skipIf`, `runIf` or `.each`: write one `it.fails` per guarantee, and loop over a table's rows inside it. The oracles:
- (a) `fullInput` renders exactly its expected document, with no warning.
- (b) The surface table: for each of the six prefixes, a spec with one element of that prefix shows the summary paragraph and the details block for `cli`, `config` and `file`, and nothing for the other three. An element with `before: null` gets the After-only block.
- (c) The title table: titles with no ` — `, with one, with two, and with a lede that already ends in `.`, `?` or `!`.
- (d) The commit table: each subject from `fullInput` lands in Fixes, in Other or in neither, as the layout says, in input order.
- (e) Upgrading: an input without the `### 4.2.0` entry renders no Upgrading section and returns exactly the warning `docs/upgrading.md has no "### 4.2.0" entry: the notes have no Upgrading section`. An entry that is the last in the file runs to the end of the file.
- (f) An intermediate plan whose spec's completing plan is in the same input joins the Plans line, whether it comes before or after that plan, and yields no Part of line.
- (g) Refusals. Two plans with `completesSpec: true` and the same `spec.path` throw exactly `<spec path> is announced in full twice: <first plan path> and <second plan path> both say completes-spec: true`. A kept element whose summary is `SURFACE_SUMMARY_PLACEHOLDER` (imported from `src/schemas/specDocument.ts`) throws exactly `<spec path>: the surface element "<surface>" still has the placeholder summary — write it before the release`. The same placeholder on an `internal:` element throws nothing.
- (h) Minimal documents: an input with no plans, no commits and no upgrading entry renders only the title and the Changes line, plus the warning. An input with only a `fix:` commit renders only Fixes after those two lines.

Each oracle must fail against the stub because the stub throws, never because an import, export or type is missing. The test file imports only `scripts/releaseNotes.ts`, `tests/unit/releaseNotes/inputs.ts`, `src/schemas/specDocument.ts` and `vitest`. A refusal oracle asserts the message with `toThrow(<exact message>)`, so the stub's not-implemented error fails it.
Before committing, run the standard gate. Every oracle must show as an expected failure, and the suite must stay green. `pnpm test:type`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm knip` must pass with the stub.
phases.boundaryContracts: Consumers: the oracle tests now, and `scripts/release-notes.ts` from phase-03. Producer: `scripts/releaseNotes.ts`. Shape: `renderReleaseNotes(ReleaseNotesInput)` returns `{ markdown, warnings }` and is pure. A refusal is a thrown `Error` carrying one of the messages in the layout arbitration. The input carries decoded facts only: the builder reads no path and runs no git.

- a spec title splits at its first spaced em dash into the heading and a sentence-cased lede — small · table · expected heading and lede per title · oracle
- each commit subject lands in Fixes, in Other or nowhere as the classification says, oldest first — small · table · classification table · oracle
- the upgrading entry is copied up to the next heading with its relative links made absolute at the tag, and a missing entry drops the section with one warning — small · example · expected section and warning text · oracle

- a section with nothing to list is left out, and the smallest notes are the title and the Changes line — small · example · expected Markdown document · oracle

tests/unit/releaseNotes/inputs.ts: the made-up inputs and the expected documents, written out by hand from the layout arbitration.

phases.title: The release notes builder
phases.objective: `renderReleaseNotes` turns the facts of a release into its notes: the Markdown the layout states, the warnings and the refusals. phase-03 then only has to gather the facts.
detailedInstructions: Implement `renderReleaseNotes` in `scripts/releaseNotes.ts` as the plan's layout arbitration states. Keep the exported types exactly as phase-01 wrote them, and keep the module pure: no file access, no git, no `process`.

Reuse `finishDocument`, `inlineCode`, `sentence` and `headingText` from `src/domain/authoring/markdown.ts`, and `SURFACE_SUMMARY_PLACEHOLDER` from `src/schemas/specDocument.ts`. Find the `### <version>` heading and the link destinations with `mdast-util-from-markdown` (already a dependency), using node offsets into the source text, so that every other byte of the entry is copied unchanged. Rewrite destinations with `posix.normalize` from `node:path`.

Read a subject's type as its leading run of letters, lower-cased, when that run is followed by an optional parenthesised scope, an optional `!`, and `: `. Any other subject is unconventional and goes to Other.

Check the refusals before rendering anything. First, duplicate full announcements, by `spec.path`, naming the first two plans in input order. Then placeholder summaries on kept elements, in input order.

Remove the `.fails` markers from `tests/unit/releaseNotes.test.ts`, and change nothing else in it or in `tests/unit/releaseNotes/inputs.ts`: the oracles provider compares their syntax trees with phase-01's commit. If an oracle cannot pass unchanged, do not adapt it. Stop, and say in the handoff which oracle fails and why.
phases.testStrategy:
- a subject's type is read with or without a scope, a breaking mark and any letter case, and anything else counts as unconventional — small · table · type per subject · in-phase
- link destinations keep a scheme or a leading slash and normalise parent segments under docs — small · table · expected destination per link · in-phase
- a fence is one backtick longer than the longest backtick run of its content and never shorter than three — small · table · fence per content · in-phase

The section renderers and their assembly with finishDocument.
Remove the it.fails markers, then add tests/unit/releaseNotesBlocks.test.ts.

Any change to the oracle assertions, the fixture inputs or the exported types.

phases.expectedHandoff: The helpers `scripts/releaseNotes.ts` now exports, with their signatures. Confirmation that the only change to the oracle files is the removal of the markers. Any oracle that could not pass unchanged, and why. Any deviation from the planned files, with the reason.

commit.subject: feat(scripts): render release notes from a release's specs, plans and commits
commit.body: Implement renderReleaseNotes: the Upgrading section copied from docs/upgrading.md with its links made absolute at the tag, each completed spec with its lede, guiding rule, plans and cli, config and file surfaces folded in details blocks, the intermediate plans, the plans without a spec, and the commits outside any run sorted into Fixes and Other. A spec announced in full twice or a placeholder summary is refused. The oracles pass with only their markers removed.

phases.title: Read a release's runs, preview its notes and write them at the cut
phases.objective: The notes of any version can be previewed from the repository with `pnpm release:notes`. The release cut writes them to `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md` in the release commit, and refuses before any write when an input is wrong.
detailedInstructions: Export `parseLog(text)`. It reads the output of `git log --reverse --no-merges --format=%H%x1f%s%x1f%B%x1e <range>` into `{ hash, subject, trailers }` records, oldest first. The trailers are the key-value lines of the body's last paragraph. They are read only when every non-blank line of that paragraph has the form `<Key>: <value>`, with a key made of letters, digits and hyphens. When a key appears twice, its first value wins. A run commit is one that carries both `Run-Id` and `Short-Name`.

Export `collectReleaseNotes(repoRoot, version)`, which returns `{ input, warnings }` as the plan's arbitrations on runs, the previous release, documents and wrong inputs state:
1. `previous` is the greatest release below `version` in `readLedger(repoRoot, "no release notes")`. With none, refuse with `no release below <version> in packages/schemas/releases.json — no release notes`.
2. Check the tag with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/tags/v<previous>`. When it is missing, refuse with `v<previous> is not a tag in <repoRoot> — fetch the tags (git fetch --tags), or clone with the full history`.
3. Read the commits with `parseLog`, over `v<previous>..HEAD`.
4. Find the candidate plans: the `*-plan.md` paths listed by `git diff --name-only --no-renames --diff-filter=A v<previous> HEAD -- docs/plans/archive`.
5. Read each candidate from the working tree:
   - its frontmatter through `readPlanFrontmatter`. `none` refuses with `<path>: no frontmatter`, and `undecodable` refuses with `<path>: <problem>`. A status other than `Completed` skips the plan without a word;
   - its title and first paragraph from the body: the first depth-1 heading's text through `mdast-util-to-string`, and the source slice of the first paragraph after that heading. With no title, refuse with `<path>: no "# " title`;
   - its run short name from its sidecar when one exists: `JSON.parse`, then `readDocumentSidecar("plan", …)`, taking `run` from the current document or from the older shape the read carries. A parse failure refuses with `<sidecar>: not JSON`, and a read error refuses with its message. Without a sidecar, the short name is `slugifyShortName(title)`.
6. Two candidates with the same short name refuse with `<plan path> and <plan path> both have the run short name <name>`.
7. Group run commits by `Short-Name`, in order of each run's first commit. A matched run adds its plan to `input.plans`. An unmatched run warns `run <short-name> names no plan completed since v<previous>: its commits are listed as commits without a run`. `input.commits` lists, in log order, the commits with no run trailers and the commits of unmatched runs.
8. A candidate that no run names warns `<plan path> was completed since v<previous>, but no run commit names <short-name>: it is not announced`.
9. For a plan whose frontmatter names a spec, look the spec up at that path, then at `archivePathFor(path)`. When `archivePathFor` throws, refuse with `<plan path>: source-spec <path> is not a spec path`. When neither path exists, refuse with `<plan path>: its source spec <path> is in neither docs/specs/ nor docs/specs/archive/`. A sidecar is read with `JSON.parse` and `readDocumentSidecar("spec", …)`, which refuse as in step 5, and gives `title`, `productGoal.guidingRule` and the `surface` fields. Without a sidecar, the spec is its `# ` title, with `guidingRule: null` and `surface: []`, and the warning `<spec path> has no sidecar: it is announced by its title alone`.
10. `upgrading` is the text of `docs/upgrading.md`. When the file is missing, refuse with `docs/upgrading.md is missing`.
11. `repository` is the constant `https://github.com/lbdremy/phax`.
Export `releaseNotes(repoRoot, version)`: `renderReleaseNotes` applied to the collected input, with the collector's warnings first and the renderer's after them.

The entry `pnpm release:notes [--root <dir>]` previews the notes of the version that `package.json` names under the root, which is the opened version. Add `"release:notes": "tsx scripts/release-notes.ts"` to `package.json`. The entry prints the Markdown on stdout and each warning on stderr as `! <warning>`. A refusal prints `✗ <message>` and exits 1. It writes nothing. Parse `--root` the way `scripts/release-cut.ts` does.

In `scripts/release.sh`, echo `writing the release notes: docs/releases/${VERSION}.md` next to the existing cut echo lines. Change the undo line to `git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd -- packages/schemas/snapshots docs/releases`. Everything else stays as it is: the cut's changed paths already reach `git add -A`.

In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, give the `ci` job's `actions/checkout` step `with: fetch-depth: 0`, with a comment saying that the release rehearsal's notes read `v<previous>..HEAD`. Leave the `security-audit` job alone.

In `tests/unit/releaseWorkflow.test.ts`, assert that the `ci` job's checkout sets `fetch-depth: 0`, that `release.sh`'s undo line cleans `docs/releases`, and that the existing release-script invariants still hold.

Never run `scripts/release.sh`, and never run the cut on the real tree. To look at real notes, run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/release-notes.ts`: agents are granted `pnpm exec tsx`, not `pnpm release:notes`. Inside the phase worktree this run's plan is not archived yet, so expect the warning about a run that names no plan. No test reads `~/.phax`, a real `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` or `~/.vibe`, or the global git config.
phases.boundaryContracts: Consumers: the cut's entry in `scripts/release-cut.ts` and the preview. Producer: `releaseNotes(repoRoot, version)` in `scripts/release-notes.ts`, which returns `{ markdown, warnings }` or throws an `Error` naming the file or the remedy. It reads git and the files under `repoRoot` and writes nothing. Consumer: `scripts/release.sh`. Producer: `cutRelease(repoRoot, version, notes)`, whose `changed` list now includes `docs/releases/<version>.md`, so the script stages the notes with the rest of the cut.
phases.testStrategy:
- run trailers in the range lead to the plan completed in the same range and to its spec at its path or in the archive — medium · example · fixture repository and expected input · in-phase
- a run naming no completed plan and a completed plan named by no run each give one warning, and the run's commits join the commits without a run — medium · example · expected warnings and commits · in-phase
- a sidecar or frontmatter that does not decode, a missing spec, a shared run short name and a missing previous tag are refused with a message naming the file or the remedy — medium · example · exact refusal messages · in-phase
- merge commits, abandoned plans and plans archived before the previous release never reach the notes — medium · example · expected input · in-phase
- trailers are read only from a body's last paragraph when every line of it is a key and a value — small · table · parsed trailers per body · in-phase
- the cut writes the notes after its other writes, lists them among the changed paths, and leaves the tree untouched when the notes file exists or the notes fail — medium · example · tree hashes before and after · in-phase
- the preview prints the notes on stdout and the warnings on stderr, and changes nothing in the repository — medium · smoke · stdout, stderr and git status · in-phase
- CI checks out the full history for the rehearsal, and the cut's undo line cleans the notes — small · example · parsed workflow and script text · in-phase
implementationOrder: collectReleaseNotes with the fixture repository helper, refusal by refusal.
releaseNotes and the preview entry, plus the package script.
cutRelease's notes parameter, the cut's entry and releaseCut.test.ts.
excludedScope: The release workflow, the GitHub Release body and .github/release.yml (phase-04).

Running scripts/release.sh, or cutting a release on the real tree.
phases.expectedHandoff: The exported functions of `scripts/release-notes.ts` and their signatures. `cutRelease`'s new signature and where it calls `notes()`. The exact warning and refusal messages, as implemented. What `pnpm exec tsx scripts/release-notes.ts` printed in the worktree, warnings included. Any deviation from the planned files, with the reason.

commit.subject: feat(scripts): read a release's runs and write its notes at the cut
commit.body: scripts/release-notes.ts reads the release's runs from the Run-Id and Short-Name trailers since the previous release's tag, matches each to the plan completed in the same range, follows source-spec to the spec and decodes the sidecars through the persisted reader, then renders the notes. pnpm release:notes previews them without writing anything. The cut takes the notes as a function called before its first write, writes docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md and stages it, and CI's checkout fetches the history its rehearsal now reads.

phases.assignmentReason: It joins git history, artifact frontmatter, the persisted sidecar reader and the release cut in one reader. A dozen refusals must fire before the cut writes anything, and no script in the repository reads git history and documents together yet.

phases.title: The notes as the GitHub release body and a docs site page
phases.objective: A release's notes reach their readers: the GitHub Release takes `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md` as its body, checked before anything is published; the docs site shows one page per release; and `docs/release.md` explains the notes and their preview.
detailedInstructions: In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, add a step named `Verify the release notes`, with `id: notes`, directly after `Prepare npm wrapper`. `Verify package versions match tag` must stay directly before `Deploy docs: guard`. The step sets `NOTES="docs/releases/${RELEASE_TAG#v}.md"`, exits 1 with a line naming the file and `scripts/release-cut.ts` when the file is missing or empty, and otherwise appends `path=${NOTES}` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`. In the `softprops/action-gh-release` step, remove `generate_release_notes`, add `body_path: ${{ steps.notes.outputs.path }}`, and rewrite the comment above it.
Delete `.github/release.yml`: only GitHub's generated notes read its categories.
In `site/build/sources.ts`, add `docs/releases` to `SOURCE_DIRECTORIES`.

In `site/build/generate.ts`, extend the map's `files` with `releaseNotePages` of the source paths before `checkPageMap`, and add that function's findings to the map findings. Use the extended map everywhere after that: navigation, link targets and the summary. In `site/build/site.ts`, make `lastModified` cover the release note sources too.

In `site/build/markdown.ts`, release-note sources get one exception. For a path under `docs/releases/`, an HTML block that is exactly `<details>`, a newline, and `<summary>TEXT</summary>` becomes `:::details TEXT`, with TEXT escaped like other text. An HTML block that is exactly `</details>` becomes `:::`. Any other raw HTML element stays a finding, in every source, `<details>` outside `docs/releases/` included.

Check the site build once by hand. Run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/release-notes.ts > docs/releases/<opened version>.md` in the worktree, then `pnpm site:build`, and confirm that the page builds with its folded blocks. Delete the file before committing, and report the result in the handoff.
In `NEXT_STEPS.md`, remove the release-notes item, and the `### Next, after the surface summaries` heading it leaves empty. The README does not describe release notes, so it stays as it is.
phases.boundaryContracts: Consumers: the release workflow's GitHub Release step and the docs site build. Producer: the `docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md` that the cut writes into the release commit. Shape: one GitHub-flavoured Markdown file per release, whose only raw HTML is the `<details>`/`<summary>` blocks the builder writes. The workflow needs the file to exist before it publishes, and the site derives one route per file from its name.
phases.testStrategy:
- the GitHub Release body is the notes file a step checks before the first publish, and GitHub generates no notes — small · example · parsed workflow and the step run under bash · in-phase
- each release notes file becomes one page at its release route, newest first in a Releases group with a nav entry, and a misnamed file is a finding — small · example · generated site files and findings · in-phase
- the details blocks of a release page become details containers, and raw HTML stays refused everywhere else — small · example · generated page text and findings · in-phase
- docs/release.md documents the notes step of the cut, the preview command and the notes as the release body — small · example · section text · in-phase
implementationOrder: release.yml's notes step and body_path, the deletion of .github/release.yml, and releaseWorkflow.test.ts.
The site: the source directory, releaseNotePages and GROUPS, the expanded map in generate.ts and site.ts, the details containers in markdown.ts, and their tests.
The one-time site build with a generated notes file, deleted again before the commit.
excludedScope: Any change to the note builder, the reader or the cut (phases 02 and 03).
A hand-written index of all releases, or one page-map entry per release.
Committing any docs/releases file: the first one is written by the 0.28.0 cut.
Any change under src/, and any change to docs-deploy.yml.
phases.verification: The `standard` gate profile in `phax.json`; its terminal `pnpm site:build` step builds the site with the new release pages code.
phases.expectedHandoff: The notes step and the release step as written. The site functions added and how a release page's route is derived. The result of the one-time `pnpm site:build` with a generated notes file: whether the folded blocks rendered, and any finding. A note that `.github/release.yml` was deleted (reconciliation lists it as planned to edit). Any deviation from the planned files, with the reason.

commit.subject: ci(release): publish the release notes as the GitHub release body and on the docs site
commit.body: The release workflow checks docs/releases/<X.Y.Z>.md before anything is published and gives it to the GitHub Release as its body; GitHub no longer generates notes, and .github/release.yml goes. The docs site renders one page per release at /releases/<X-Y-Z>, newest first under Releases, with the notes' details blocks as Rspress containers. docs/release.md documents the notes and pnpm release:notes, and NEXT_STEPS.md drops the item.
